key_insight: The paper shows that improvements in language-model-based entity matching cannot be attributed to architecture alone; backbone, pretraining variant, and model size all interact and must be controlled separately. By disentangling these factors, it identifies what actually drives performance gains.
problem_solved: Prior entity-matching studies often mix together different matcher architectures, model backbones, model variants, and sizes, making it unclear which design choices really improve results.
method: Runs a controlled factorial study over entity-matching setups to isolate architecture effects from backbone, variant, and size.
Compares bi-encoder, cross-encoder, and generative matcher architectures under matched experimental conditions.
Analyzes performance differences systematically to identify the true sources of gains.
impact: This gives practitioners a clearer basis for choosing and tuning language models for entity matching. It reduces misleading comparisons and helps teams invest in the model choices that genuinely improve accuracy and efficiency.
visual_elements: A comparison matrix showing architecture vs. backbone vs. size vs. variant
A flow diagram of bi-encoder, cross-encoder, and generative matching pipelines
Bar charts of performance under controlled experimental settings
An icon-based summary separating confounding factors into distinct layers
paper_title: Beyond Scale and Generation: Understanding Language Model-based Entity Matching
paper_authors: Zeyu Zhang, Xue Li, Iacer Calixto, Paul Groth, Sebastian Schelter
